return 0; }","note":"When the fuzz target later queries chain certs, BoringSSL lazily caches the chain into ctx->cert->x509_chain before returning it."},{"step":5,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/boringssl/ssl/ssl_x509.cc","function":"SSL_CTX_get0_chain_certs","line":903,"var":"*out_chain","code":"*out_chain = ctx->cert->x509_chain;","note":"The cached chain pointer is written to the caller-provided out parameter, propagating the certificate-chain object into the API consumer."},{"step":6,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/boringssl/fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":337,"var":"chains","code":"SSL_CTX_get0_chain_certs(ctx, &chains);","note":"The fuzz target invokes the getter on the same SSL_CTX, exercising the chain-caching path and the returned pointer flow under MSan."},{"step":7,"file":"repo-vul/src-vul/boringssl/fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc","function":"LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput","line":544,"var":"ssl","code":"bssl::UniquePtr<SSL> ssl(SSL_new(ctx.get()));","note":"The target then creates an SSL object from the mutated context, which consumes the context state and reaches the memory-safety sink where the reported uninitialized-value issue manifests."}]
